_meta.what_this_is: The same 30 cases from evals-basic-01, each carrying two PASS/FAIL verdicts: 'human' is the gold verdict (the basic-01 rubric's clean/not-clean, treated here as ground truth), and 'judge' is an LLM judge's PASS/FAIL on the same answer. The question of this module: can we trust the judge? Measured by how well its column agrees with the human column.
_meta.human_is: The gold label. In basic-01 a case was clean (6/6 checks) or not; clean -> PASS, otherwise FAIL. 19 PASS, 11 FAIL.
_meta.judge_is: A FIXTURE standing in for one LLM judge call per case (PASS/FAIL against a rubric prompt). Stored, not generated, so judge.py runs offline with no key and prints the same numbers every time. A real calibration run would call a model, cost money, and vary; the point of the module is that you must measure whatever it returns before trusting it.
_meta.the_judge_is_lenient: By construction this judge passes 23 of 30 while the humans pass 19: it misses 5 of the 11 answers that should fail, and false-alarms once (fails F08, which humans passed). That leniency is exactly what raw agreement hides and what the calibration report exposes.
